description: Two-dimensional evidence model. Axis A = provenance (where the number came from). Axis B = purpose (what the number was built to measure). Source authenticity and schedule applicability are separate judgements; an official source never earns a high planning confidence on its own.

axis_a_notes.A0: Engine defaults and any value with no external source. Never upgraded by this layer.
axis_a_notes.A1: Government quota, labour norm or published standard. High source authenticity, but usually built for cost/budget consumption, not for schedule planning.
axis_a_notes.A2: Contractor or industry benchmark supplied outside a verified project record.
axis_a_notes.A3: Measured actuals from a named project with accepted quantity and timesheet labour.
axis_a_notes.A4: A rate derived from a reviewed A3 population. Requires sample size, scope and unit compatibility.

axis_b_purpose.budget_consumption: Labour days allowed per unit for pricing. Includes allowance/幅度差 and is not a site production rate.
axis_b_purpose.planning_benchmark: A rate whose declared purpose is schedule planning or duration estimating.
axis_b_purpose.observed_production: Measured output per worker-day from a real site record.
axis_b_purpose.calibrated_production: A planning rate derived from a compatible observed population.

scope_equivalence_classes.exact: Same work content boundary as the target activity; no work belonging to another activity type and no missing component.
scope_equivalence_classes.partial: Same activity boundary, but a declared design condition (grade, size class, spacing, thickness, layer count, access type) is not declared in the target scope.
scope_equivalence_classes.composite: Spans more than one activity type; cannot be attributed to a single activity without splitting.
scope_equivalence_classes.not_comparable: No comparable engine activity, or the item is a delta/increment rather than a complete activity.

schedule_applicability_classes.direct: Scope closely matches the site planning activity and the item may become a planning benchmark candidate.
schedule_applicability_classes.adjusted: Scope is broadly aligned but a conversion or condition factor is required before it can be used.
schedule_applicability_classes.reference_only: Usable as a sanity check; must not enter a selected planning rate.
schedule_applicability_classes.rejected: Scope, unit or definition cannot be compared reliably.

applicability_guardrails.guardrail_reason: An A1 budget-consumption item is priced labour, not site production. Marking it direct would convert a cost allowance into a schedule rate without evidence.

day_basis.note: Standard workday is 8 hours. A source using a different day length is rescaled by standard_hours / source_hours. Actual recorded hours in A3 data are never rescaled.

note: Required fields are validated but a missing locator is a data gap, never a reason to invent a value.
